maps.title: Arabia · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Standard land opening; adapt to resource positions

cards.title: 1 · Exposed resources change the spending order
cards.body: With forward wood/gold, fund a range/stable and defense before banking for Castle. Small walls stop melee units; archers require units or another woodline.

cards.title: 2 · Scout the opening during the age-up
cards.body: Scout military buildings and the first army during the Feudal transition. Continued deer pushing can leave the first defensive range too late. See civilization guides for transitions.

maps.title: Arena · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Stone walls, Fast Castle and relic investment

cards.title: 1 · Relics: stable first, monastery on arrival
cards.body: For scout relic play, advance with stable + blacksmith. Prepare scouts during the age-up; reserve 175 wood for a monastery and 100 gold for the first monk before extra TCs.

cards.title: 2 · Forward towers or castles change the boom
cards.body: Forward towers/castles call for inner access to wood/gold before extra TCs. Use the tower- or castle-defense page for allocations and units.

maps.title: Socotra · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Close quarters; six herdables, one elephant, five small huntables

cards.title: 1 · Secure the only elephant first
cards.body: Usually six herdables, one elephant and five small huntables. Locate and lure the elephant before deer pushing; there is no second boar.

cards.title: 2 · Plan the food bridge earlier
cards.body: Plan the next deer/berry mill before the elephant runs out. If it is stolen, bridge with berries/farms and a later Men-at-Arms timing.

cards.title: 3 · Contact can happen in Dark Age
cards.body: Villagers or militia can arrive in Dark Age. Research Loom before villager fights; prepare resource walls and the barracks during the age-up.

maps.title: Scandinavia · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Three large huntables; land pressure and separate lakes

cards.title: 1 · Find the third large huntable
cards.body: Three large huntables, deer and small animals extend the opening. Keep herdables as a bridge; delay mass farming while safe natural food funds fishing and military.

cards.title: 2 · One-dock practice opening
cards.body: Practice baseline: dock at villager 11–13, then three or four fish. About five or six woodcutters cover fishing, not buildings. Shift food workers to wood when fish can cover food.

cards.title: 3 · Attack the other lake with a land builder
cards.body: Send a land builder to dock the other lake. Shelter threatened fishing ships in your dock; it fires no arrows in Dark Age. Reserve warship resources too.

maps.title: Nomad · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Two builders on the TC, one on the dock; check neighbors

cards.title: 1 · Two villagers build the TC; one builds a dock
cards.body: Two nearby villagers build the TC by wood/food; the third docks and gathers shore fish. Reserve 150 wood + 75 for the first boat; do not delay the TC for perfect mines.

cards.title: 2 · Fish count depends on the next investment
cards.body: Three or four fish can suit a close-dock fast Feudal. Safe back docks permit more. Five or six woodcutters cover one fishing dock; warships and another dock cost extra.

cards.title: 3 · Nearby neighbors may rule out a greedy Fast Castle
cards.body: Use herdables to locate neighbors/docks. A close TC or tower pressure on wood/gold favors Feudal investment; unique-unit Fast Castle needs safe gathering space.

cards.title: 4 · Give fishing ships a route back to the dock
cards.body: A standard dock shelters five fishing ships: no Dark Age arrows, at most three in Feudal. Front docks contest space; back docks favor short fishing and retreat routes.

maps.title: Land Nomad · Map tips
maps.subtitle: No starting TC or fishing economy; hunt into Castle

cards.title: 1 · Build near wood and usable food
cards.body: Build promptly with two or three nearby villagers beside wood/hunt. There is no fishing boom; use herdables to find more food and enemy TCs.

cards.title: 2 · Use hunt while it remains defendable
cards.body: Plan the next hunting group and mill together. Against nearby pressure, farm under the TC rather than relying on denied hunting routes.

cards.title: 3 · Let spawn positions choose the investment
cards.body: Distant enemies favor Fast Castle; a TC beside your wood calls for Feudal defense. Place the next TC on usable food and wood/gold.

maps.title: African Clearing · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Shore-fish economy; not a sea-Nomad dock opening

cards.title: 1 · Place the TC by shore fish and outer wood
cards.body: Build by a pond near wood. Villagers gather shore fish directly: no dock or fishing ships needed. Fund mills and military buildings instead.

cards.title: 2 · Prepare the next pond before moving the workers
cards.body: Before the pond runs out, send one mill builder, then roughly four to six fishers. Farm if enemy pressure denies the next pond.

cards.title: 3 · Mobility contests the food economy
cards.body: Scouts contest dispersed ponds, with knights/camels as Castle options. A unique-unit Fast Castle still needs military spending to protect exposed fishers.

maps.title: Steppe · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Six villagers, no TC; tents provide population space

cards.title: 1 · Build the TC before houses
cards.body: Standard civilizations start with six villagers, no TC and tents for population. Build the TC promptly with the starting group; scout for food instead of making two opening houses.

cards.title: 2 · Food first, then establish wood income
cards.body: After the TC finishes, use about six villagers on nearby food and build toward three or four woodcutters. Berries/hunt bridge a missing-sheep start.

cards.title: 3 · Use actual population; expect a different clock
cards.body: A 19-pop build still means actual population 19. TC construction changes the clock; separately budget the barracks and mining camp before Feudal.

maps.title: MegaRandom · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Opening and economy adjustments. Counts are practice starting points; adapt to your civilization, resources and pressure.

cards.title: 1 · Inspect your starting setup
cards.body: In the first roughly 30 seconds, check villagers, units, buildings, stockpile and population cap. Fill immediate gaps instead of applying a fixed-population build blindly.

cards.title: 2 · Adapt food and wood
cards.body: Use extra hunt; consider a dock and more woodcutters with safe fish. With little hunt, transition earlier to berries/farms.

cards.title: 3 · Check connections
cards.body: Locate shallows, gaps and special buildings. Do not infer a safe Fast Castle from appearance alone.

cards.title: 4 · Team games: share starting information
cards.body: Report unusual starts and terrain. Divide water/land roles by distance rather than assuming flank/pocket roles.

maps.title: Glade · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Usually only four home gold tiles; expansion is beyond the exit

cards.title: 1 · Wall the opening and plan the next gold
cards.body: Wall the entrance for Fast Castle. Home gold is usually four tiles, about 3,200 gold. Locate the next mine outside during the age-up.

cards.title: 2 · Buy space before committing to extra TCs
cards.body: Contest the exit with army/monks before expanding. Unique units into a one-TC fast Imperial is an option; add TCs once outside resources are accessible.

cards.title: 3 · Use a forward castle to secure the expansion
cards.body: Use the first castle to cover the exit, outside gold and forward ground. A castle lock favors Imperial trebuchets over repeatedly adding Castle Age units.

maps.title: Enclosed · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Unbuildable rocky path; usually only two home stone tiles

cards.title: 1 · The rocky path cannot hold emergency defenses
cards.body: The rocky ring cannot hold walls/towers. Find buildable space for mining camps/TCs before moving miners; emergency defenses must stand off the path.

cards.title: 2 · Budget the small home stone deposit
cards.body: Usually seven home gold tiles and two stone tiles, about 700 stone. Budget the first castle and TCs; a second castle needs outside stone.

cards.title: 3 · Forest cover does not secure the outer route
cards.body: Enemies can circle around the forest. Production near the exits supports outside mines; reopen a blocked reinforcement route before sending more workers.

maps.title: Fortified Clearing · Map tips
maps.subtitle: A starting front wall; rear access and outside mines

cards.title: 1 · Inspect the rear before treating the base as closed
cards.body: The starting wall covers only part of the approach. Inspect rear routes before Fast Castle; spend wall wood on actual gaps.

cards.title: 2 · Expand toward the next mine
cards.body: Secondary mines may be outside the wall. Scout them during the age-up and use the next TC/castle to secure mines and wood.

maps.title: Hideout · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Palisade start; two approaches and an outer ring

cards.title: 1 · Check for a wall-off before Castle Age
cards.body: Scout exits before Feudal to catch a wall-off. Militia can contest builders; established walls with ranged support favor using the other approach.

cards.title: 2 · Archer-tower pressure changes the inner layout
cards.body: Against archer-tower pressure, rewall outside range, relocate workers or counter-tower to preserve access. Protect the Castle timing; use the tower-defense guide.

cards.title: 3 · Expand through an exit and narrow the late-game front
cards.body: Extend monasteries, production and TCs through an exit. In late Castle Age, stonewall one side to concentrate the army on the other.

maps.title: Fortress · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Ten villagers, a castle and starting farms

cards.title: 1 · Use the ten-villager start and five farms
cards.body: Standard random-map settings give ten villagers, a castle and five farms. Assign farms, hunt and wood immediately; the larger workforce changes the age-up timing.

cards.title: 2 · A unique-unit opening needs no first-castle stone
cards.body: No 650-stone investment is needed for the first castle. Fund unique units/upgrades directly, or use it for defense while the next TC secures outside wood/gold.

cards.title: 3 · The existing castle supports a fast Imperial
cards.body: The castle satisfies the building prerequisite for Imperial; Castle still needs two Feudal buildings. Check existing facilities first and use the castle for immediate trebuchets.

maps.title: Black Forest · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Choke-point walling; safe hunt and optional fish ponds

cards.title: 1 · Pay for early walling only when contesting space
cards.body: Contested forward walls can justify Loom, two villagers and the scout. Otherwise wall a safe choke; leave room for a second layer against enemy builders.

cards.title: 2 · Check the pond before changing the build
cards.body: Dock plus three fishing ships costs 375 wood. A poor/distant pond favors hunt into farms; a chosen fish boom needs its own extra Dark Age wood.

cards.title: 3 · Choose siege timing or another route
cards.body: A castle-locked choke favors trebuchets. The Mangonel line needs Onager to cut trees; Khmer Ballista Elephants can cut a Castle Age flank earlier.

maps.title: Michi · Map tips
maps.subtitle: A forest barrier; plan the cut timing and composition

cards.title: 1 · The cutting unit sets the contact timing
cards.body: Conventional cuts use Imperial Onagers. Khmer Ballista Elephants can cut in Castle Age, so military preparation may need to come earlier.

cards.title: 2 · Build production and upgrades during the age-up
cards.body: Add production and upgrades during the age-up; prepare the army before cutting. Bombard Cannons need a university/workshops beforehand and Chemistry on arrival.

cards.title: 3 · Keep trade clear of the planned attack route
cards.body: Reserve a rear trade route between opposite-end markets. Keep the planned cut and reinforcement corridor clear of houses and markets.

maps.title: Amazon Tunnel · Map tips
maps.subtitle: One main tunnel; forests can still be cut

cards.title: 1 · Wall the shared route, not every individual base
cards.body: Identify the tunnel connecting the teams and coordinate one choke-point wall line. Rewall behind tower pressure to preserve gathering space.

cards.title: 2 · A locked tunnel calls for siege or a forest route
cards.body: Break a castle lock with Imperial siege or an Onager flank. Khmer Ballista Elephants can create a Castle Age forest route earlier.

cards.title: 3 · Use limited fighting space for complementary units
cards.body: Keep the rear trade route open. Limited choke space favors complementary frontline, ranged and siege roles over every player massing the same melee unit.

maps.title: Oasis · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Central wood; two routes around the outside

cards.title: 1 · A wood TC does not close the outer ring
cards.body: A second TC can secure central wood/mines. Both outer routes lead to enemies; close both approaches or connect walls to the edge.

cards.title: 2 · Close one route before concentrating on the other
cards.body: Close the unused route before concentrating on one side. Assign both ends in team games and keep trade behind those defenses.

maps.title: Four Lakes · Map tips
maps.subtitle: One-lake fishing opening; offensive docks and a second lake

cards.title: 1 · A conservative one-dock baseline
cards.body: Generic baseline: dock at villager 11–13, three or four fish. Dock + three boats costs 375 wood; five or six woodcutters cover fishing, not buildings. Lithuanian early docks use a separate build.

cards.title: 2 · Shift workers when fishing covers food
cards.body: When fish cover food, move some food workers to wood. For Fast Castle, pause new boats if needed to reserve 325 wood for market + blacksmith.

cards.title: 3 · A forward builder is the route into another lake
cards.body: Other lakes require a land builder and a new dock. Watch for enemy builders; shelter fishing ships in docks, with no Dark Age arrows and at most three in Feudal.

cards.title: 4 · Fund the second lake alongside the land army
cards.body: If the first lake still feeds a land battle, fund the army first. Add a second dock with one builder when affordable, then start with a few boats.

maps.title: Islands · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Front-dock distance sets the Feudal timing; back docks shelter fish

cards.title: 1 · Close docks favor an earlier military timing
cards.body: Three or four fish can be a fast-Feudal baseline. Reserve 150 wood for a second dock plus fleet resources. Close docks favor earlier army; distant back docks permit more fish.

cards.title: 2 · Use the current naval counters and dock protection
cards.body: Hulks counter Fire Galleys but are vulnerable to Galleys. Shelter threatened fish; Feudal docks fire at most three arrows, changing fights under them.

cards.title: 3 · Convert water control into a next step
cards.body: Use a fleet lead to deny docks/fishing, then choose Castle naval pressure or a landing. Transports and land production need separate wood.

maps.title: Team Islands · Map tips
maps.subtitle: A shared island; coordinate front and back docks

cards.title: 1 · Assign the first naval fight
cards.body: Front players fund fast Feudal and a second dock; distant back docks can add fish. Assign the first naval wave instead of everyone choosing a delayed opening.

cards.title: 2 · Maintain production through the age transition
cards.body: Keep reinforcing the front. Medium Warships upgrades the Galley, Fire Galley and Hulk lines together in Castle Age, giving a mixed fleet a shared upgrade timing.

cards.title: 3 · A landing bypasses the naval front
cards.body: Assign one player a land response to enemy builders/production while others hold water. Avoid abandoning the naval front with the whole team.

maps.title: Migration · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Small starting islands; transport and a central foothold

cards.title: 1 · Long sailing distances can support Fast Castle
cards.body: Scout the mainland before island resources run low. Long sailing distances and safe back docks can support fish into Fast Castle; an early landing changes military needs.

cards.title: 2 · Reserve 400 wood and 100 stone for the move
cards.body: Transport + TC costs 400 wood and 100 stone for standard civilizations. Scout in Feudal, send roughly four to six builders when safe, and place the TC on Castle arrival.

cards.title: 3 · Choose a foothold that can sustain production
cards.body: The first mainland TC should secure wood/gold and production space. A resource-poor beach needs another move; choose a different landing if the shore is blocked.

maps.title: Northern Isles · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Naval fighting and early landings

cards.title: 1 · Choose the first investment: fleet or landing
cards.body: Naval opening: three or four fish and a second dock during the age-up. A landing needs transport/land-production wood instead. Fund a coherent first attack.

cards.title: 2 · A rear landing needs a land response
cards.body: Transports can bypass the fleet. Deal with landed builders and the first production building before a protected range/stable forces a costly land transition.

cards.title: 3 · Use actual sailing distance for the age-up
cards.body: Close docks favor fast Feudal; distant back docks allow more fish. Reserve fleet resources near enemy docks and shelter threatened fish; Dark Age docks fire no arrows.

maps.title: Gold Rush · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Central hill gold; establish position before mining

cards.title: 1 · Keep early foot units out of the central predators
cards.body: Predators occupy the central hill. Route militia and forward builders around it, preserving health and arrival timing.

cards.title: 2 · Castle Age army secures the hill
cards.body: Use home gold for the first army. One or two TCs preserve military spending; secure the hill before moving miners.

cards.title: 3 · Prepare stone for a useful high-ground castle
cards.body: For a central castle, start roughly three or four stone miners on Castle arrival. Cover gold and uphill access; denied players can contest outer hills or flank before trebuchets.

maps.title: Golden Pit · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Central low-ground gold; defend from the rim

cards.title: 1 · Use home gold for the opening
cards.body: Use a standard land opening and pressure home resources when possible. Plan pit access as home gold declines; center rushes and fast Imperial are options, not defaults.

cards.title: 2 · A castle plan starts with gradual stone income
cards.body: A castle plan can start with three or four stone miners on arrival. A rim castle covering gold/access need not stand in the deepest center.

cards.title: 3 · Protect the uphill route out of the pit
cards.body: Keep the army on the rim and protect miners’ exit. If a castle denies gold, cover another section or prepare trebuchets rather than repeatedly attacking uphill.

maps.title: Yucatan · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Extra hunt and berries; plan the next natural-food source

cards.title: 1 · Extra natural food changes the wood budget
cards.body: Extra hunt/berries can delay farms and free wood for military buildings or another lumber camp while safe food sustains production.

cards.title: 2 · Move to a prepared food source
cards.body: Prepare a safe mill before TC food runs out, then move roughly four to six workers. Enemy scouts on outside routes can make farms preferable.

cards.title: 3 · Check the walking route before choosing early aggression
cards.body: Forest can turn a short straight-line distance into a long march. Scout the route before choosing Men-at-Arms; a detour gives opponents time to wall.

maps.title: Arabian Desert · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Sparse woodlines; deer and small-animal variants

cards.title: 1 · Budget a mill for small-animal variants
cards.body: Fewer deer or small-animal variants may need a 100-wood mill. Budget it before mill, barracks and mining camp compete for the final Dark Age wood.

cards.title: 2 · Choose a second woodline during the age-up
cards.body: For small/exposed forests, scout a second woodline and reserve 100 wood during the age-up. Prefer a different approach so one archer group cannot deny both.

cards.title: 3 · Thin woodlines need a response to archers
cards.body: Small walls stop melee. Archers hitting thin woodlines call for skirmishers or a move; longer walls can simply delay the first defensive units.

maps.title: Haboob · Map tips
maps.subtitle: Distant exposed wood; defend it with army

cards.title: 1 · Locate the first usable forest early
cards.body: Substantial forests are far from the TC’s straggler trees. Scout a usable line before sending woodcutters or exhausting the stragglers.

cards.title: 2 · Army takes priority over an expensive full wall
cards.body: Full walls are costly. For Men-at-Arms into skirmishers, prioritize the range and first skirmishers over long outer walls; small walls only stop melee.

cards.title: 3 · Have a second woodline ready before archers arrive
cards.body: Reserve 100 wood and scout another forest during the age-up. If archers deny the first, open the next camp with one builder; a second TC can secure it in Castle.
